ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A panel is composed of 4 circles. When Lucy touches a circle, this circle and the others that touch this circle change their color from white to black or from black to white, as shown in the picture. Starting with all white circles, at least how many circles must Lucy touch, one after the other, so that all circles turn black?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are 4 circles in the figure, arranged in a 2×2 square. In the schematic diagram, after the finger touches the upper-left circle, the upper-left circle and the upper-right circle and lower-left circle that are in contact with it all undergo black-white flipping, while the lower-right circle has no change, indicating that one touch will flip the touched circle and the circles adjacent and in contact with it up, down, left, and right, a total of 3 circles. Reasoning: Starting from 4 all-white circles. First prove that 4 times can do it: touch each of the 4 circles once. For any one circle, it will flip 1 time because it itself is touched, and will also flip 1 time each because the two circles adjacent to it are touched respectively; the circle diagonally opposite to it is not in contact and does not affect it. Therefore each circle flips a total of 3 times, and after an odd number of flips it changes from white to black, so 4 times can certainly make all circles become black. Then prove that fewer than 4 times will not work: 0 times is of course all white; 1 time can only flip 3 circles, leaving 1 white circle; when 2 times, the flipping regions corresponding to the two touches must overlap, and the overlapping circle will be flipped twice and return to its original color, so in the end it is impossible to get 4 black circles, and at most 2 black circles are left; when 3 times, each time flipping 3 circles will change the parity of the number of black circles once, and starting from 0 black circles, after 3 times the number of black circles should be odd, while 4 black circles is even, impossible. Therefore at least 4 times are needed.

method.method_draft: 先看图：面板上只有4个圆，呈方形相邻；示意图说明一次触摸会让被摸的圆和与它接触的圆一起翻转颜色。再看文字：从全白开始，要尽量少地连续触摸，使四个圆都变黑。先给出一个上界：把四个圆各摸一次。因为每个圆在这个方形里都被自己和另外两个相邻圆影响，共被翻转3次，奇数次翻转后就是黑色，所以4次一定能成功。再证不能少于4次：1次显然只有3个圆变黑，不够；2次时，无论摸哪两个圆，两个触摸的翻转区域都会有重叠，重叠部分会被翻两次又回到白色，所以最后最多只能留下2个黑圆；3次时，每次翻转3个圆，黑圆总数的奇偶性会是奇数，不可能正好得到4个黑圆。于是最少必须摸4次。
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有4个圆，排列成2×2的方形。示意图里手指触摸左上圆后，左上圆以及与它相接触的右上圆、左下圆都发生黑白翻转，而右下圆没有变化，说明一次触摸会翻转被摸的圆和它上下左右相邻接触的圆，共3个圆。

推理：从4个全白圆开始。先证明4次可以做到：把4个圆各触摸一次。对于任意一个圆，它会因为自己被摸而翻转1次，又会因为与它相邻的两个圆分别被摸而各翻转1次；与它斜对角的圆不接触，不影响它。所以每个圆总共翻转3次，奇数次翻转后由白变黑，因此4次一定能让全部圆变黑。

再证明少于4次不行：0次当然全白；1次只能翻转3个圆，剩下1个白圆；2次时，两次触摸对应的翻转区域必有重叠，重叠的圆会被翻转两次回到原色，最终不可能得到4个黑圆，最多留下2个黑圆；3次时，每次翻转3个圆，会使黑圆个数的奇偶性改变一次，从0个黑圆开始，3次后黑圆个数应为奇数，而4个黑圆是偶数，不可能。因此最少需要4次。

method.method_draft: 先读图像：四个圆排成2×2方形；示意图中摸左上圆后，左上圆及与它相接的右上、左下圆翻色，而斜对角的右下圆不变，所以相邻关系是方形四条边。再读文字：从全白开始，求使四个圆都变黑的最少触摸次数。用模2方程建模：设左上、右上、左下、右下四个圆分别被摸的奇偶次数为a,b,c,d。重复摸同一圆两次会抵消，所以只需考虑0或1。要最终全黑，每个圆被翻转次数都必须为奇数，因此有方程：左上 a+b+c=1；右上 b+a+d=1；左下 c+a+d=1；右下 d+b+c=1（均在mod 2下）。由前两个方程得c=d；由左下方程得a=1；由右下方程得b=1；再代回左上得c=1，所以d=1。唯一可行方案是四个圆都摸奇数次，最少就是每个摸一次，共4次。
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中四个圆排成一个2×2的方形布局。示意中手触摸左上圆后，左上圆自身变色，同时与它相接的右上圆、左下圆也变色；斜对角的右下圆不变。因此可知“相接”的关系是方形的四条边相邻，不包括对角线相邻。

再推理：从全白开始，要让四个圆最终全黑，就是每个圆都要被翻转奇数次。设左上、右上、左下、右下四个圆被触摸的奇偶次数分别为a,b,c,d，其中每个变量按mod 2计算，只需考虑0或1，因为同一个圆摸两次效果会抵消。

根据相邻关系，各圆被翻转次数为：左上圆被a,b,c影响，所以a+b+c=1；右上圆被b,a,d影响，所以b+a+d=1；左下圆被c,a,d影响，所以c+a+d=1；右下圆被d,b,c影响，所以d+b+c=1，均在mod 2下。

由前两个方程相减或相加得c=d。把d=c代入左下方程c+a+d=1，得到c+a+c=1，即a=1。把d=c代入右下方程d+b+c=1，得到c+b+c=1，即b=1。再代入左上方程a+b+c=1，得到1+1+c=1，所以c=1，因此d=1。

所以四个圆都必须被摸奇数次。为了次数最少，每个圆各摸一次，共4次。

When Lucy touches a circle, this circle and the others that touch this circle change their color from white to black or from black to white, as shown in the picture. Starting with all white circles, at least how many circles must Lucy touch, one after the other, so that all circles turn black?

When Lucy touches a circle, this circle and the others that touch this circle change their color from white to black or from black to white, as shown in the picture. Starting with all white circles, at least how many circles must Lucy touch, one after the other, so that all circles turn black?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: There are 4 circles in the figure, arranged in a 2×2 square. In the schematic diagram, after the finger touches the upper-left circle, the upper-left circle and the upper-right circle and lower-left circle that are in contact with it all undergo black-white flipping, while the lower-right circle has no change, indicating that one touch will flip the touched circle and the circles adjacent and in contact with it up, down, left, and right, a total of 3 circles.

Reasoning: Starting from 4 all-white circles. First prove that 4 times can do it: touch each of the 4 circles once. For any one circle, it will flip 1 time because it itself is touched, and will also flip 1 time each because the two circles adjacent to it are touched respectively; the circle diagonally opposite to it is not in contact and does not affect it. Therefore each circle flips a total of 3 times, and after an odd number of flips it changes from white to black, so 4 times can certainly make all circles become black.

Then prove that fewer than 4 times will not work: 0 times is of course all white; 1 time can only flip 3 circles, leaving 1 white circle; when 2 times, the flipping regions corresponding to the two touches must overlap, and the overlapping circle will be flipped twice and return to its original color, so in the end it is impossible to get 4 black circles, and at most 2 black circles are left; when 3 times, each time flipping 3 circles will change the parity of the number of black circles once, and starting from 0 black circles, after 3 times the number of black circles should be odd, while 4 black circles is even, impossible. Therefore at least 4 times are needed.
